observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver is copied out of ECX at 0x005dc316 (MOV ESI,ECX) and immediately used as a base for two LEA instructions, while the single argument is read from the caller's stack at [ESP + 0xc] after two pushes (0x005dc312). The terminal instruction is RET 0x4 at 0x005dc334, so the callee pops the one argument word. Note the odd stack discipline: the argument is fetched AFTER 'push esi; push edi', so [ESP + 0xc] resolves to the caller's [ESP + 4] -- a fact that only holds if the two pushes are counted.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the EAX produced by the last 0x008105b0 call that executed: the +0x14 sub-object's answer when it was non-null, otherwise the +0x2c sub-object's answer (which may itself be null)
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x005dc323 TEST EAX,EAX and 0x005dc325 JNZ read the first call's EAX; when the branch is not taken the second call at 0x005dc32d leaves its own answer in EAX. Neither POP EDI (0x005dc332) nor POP ESI (0x005dc333) touches EAX, and the epilogue is only those two pops plus RET. The Ghidra decompilation types this function 'void' and drops the result entirely; that typing is a decompiler miss, contradicted by every inspected caller.

observed_mechanics: 0x005dc310 / 0x005dc311: PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI -- the only register preservation, and the reason the argument read at 0x005dc312 uses [ESP + 0xc]
0x005dc312: MOV EDI,dword ptr [ESP + 0xc] -- with ESP already lowered by 8, this is the caller's first stack argument
0x005dc316: MOV ESI,ECX -- the receiver is parked in ESI and used as a base for both LEAs
0x005dc318 / 0x005dc31a: PUSH 0x1 / PUSH EDI -- the callee is thiscall with two stack arguments; the constant 1 is the second, the id the first
0x005dc31b: LEA ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x14] -- first candidate: the sub-object at receiver + 0x14
0x005dc31e: CALL 0x008105b0 -- the entire search for the first candidate
0x005dc323 / 0x005dc325: TEST EAX,EAX / JNZ 0x005dc332 -- short-circuit on a NON-NULL answer, so the fallback runs only on a null or empty result
0x005dc327..0x005dc32d: the identical PUSH 0x1 / PUSH EDI / LEA ECX,[ESI + 0x2c] / CALL 0x008105b0 sequence for the sub-object at receiver + 0x2c
0x005dc332 / 0x005dc333: POP EDI / POP ESI -- neither touches EAX, which is why the function is a forwarding return
0x005dc334: RET 0x4 -- the callee pops the one argument word

0x008105b0 body: MOV ECX,[ECX + 0x14] / TEST ECX,ECX / JZ -> XOR EAX,EAX / RET 0x8, otherwise JMP 0x00810200. It is a two-instruction gate: if the receiver's own +0x14 pointer is null the answer is a hard zero with no search at all; otherwise it TAIL-TRANSFERS to 0x00810200 with the two stack arguments forwarded in place and the pointer already dereferenced.

0x00810200 body: walks the pointer array at [receiver + 100] up to [receiver + 0x68]; for each entry it calls vtable slot +0xc with the literal 0xeeee8218, keeps the answer, calls vtable slot +0x1c and compares the result against the requested id, and on a miss, when the flag is non-zero, calls vtable slot +0xf0 with (id, 1) and returns that answer instead. Returns null when the array is empty or nothing matches.
0xeeee8218 is UTFWin::IWindow::TYPE: Spore/UTFWin/IWindow.h line 91 declares 'static const uint32_t TYPE = 0xEEEE8218'. This is the only constant in the search path that the SDK pins down.

0x00810200's `parameter 100` is 0x64, and its array bound +0x68; those are fields of the object the +0x14 pointer designates, i.e. of UTFWin::UILayout's mpLayoutObjects target. The SDK records UILayoutObjects::mRootComponents at +0x5c, which does NOT line up with the observed +0x64/+0x68; the discrepancy is recorded in unresolved_questions rather than reconciled.

semantic_contract: Two-candidate UI element lookup keyed by a 32-bit control id. Try the sub-object at receiver + 0x14 first; if and only if that returns null, try the sub-object at receiver + 0x2c; return whichever answer the last executed search produced, including null. Both searches are made with the same literal flag 1, which the SDK's UILayout::FindWindowByID spells as its bRecursive parameter. Each search is gated on the sub-object's own +0x14 pointer and, when that is non-null, is a linear scan of an element array that filters elements to UTFWin::IWindow (class id 0xEEEE8218), compares an id returned by vtable slot +0x1c, and on a miss retries through vtable slot +0xf0 with (id, 1). The receiver is the EditorUI aggregate, not a single layout, and the answer is a pointer that callers immediately dispatch vtable slot +0x7c on -- so the function is a find-by-control-id over the editor's window hierarchy, and the return value is live even though the decompiler typed it void.
classification_rationale: The behaviour of this body is fully observed -- 17 instructions, one conditional, two calls, exact push order, and the return-in-EAX semantics recovered from the epilogue plus twelve callsites. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because material elements remain bounded, and each is named: (1) the three virtual slots the search dispatches through have no concrete callee, since the element type is only known at runtime; (2) the array bounds observed inside 0x00810200 (+0x64 / +0x68 of the layout-objects target) do not reconcile with the SDK's declared UILayoutObjects::mRootComponents at +0x5c, so the container that is being scanned is bounded rather than established; (3) whether slot +0xf0 is a recursive descent or a sibling lookup is an inference from its (id, 1) argument shape, not an observation. The owning class of the receiver is corroborated by the cEditor + 0x78 field the SDK names mpEditorUI and by the +0x14/+0x2c spacing matching ASSERT_SIZE(UILayout, 0x18), which is why this is BOUNDED_SEMANTIC and not STILL_UNKNOWN -- but the bound is named above.
semantic_findings: 0x005dc310 returns a pointer. The decompiler's 'void' is wrong: neither POP touches EAX, and twelve callsites read EAX and dereference it immediately.
It is a two-candidate fallback, not a loop: the +0x14 sub-object is tried, and only a null answer reaches the +0x2c sub-object. The branch polarity is JNZ-to-end, i.e. short-circuit on success.
The receiver is the EditorUI aggregate. cEditor + 0x78 is read at 0x0058c7db, the SDK names that field mpEditorUI, and the two searched offsets are 0x18 apart, exactly ASSERT_SIZE(UILayout, 0x18).

The +0x14 and +0x2c sub-objects are UILayout by-value members whose own +0x14 is mpLayoutObjects. 0x008105b0's whole body is the null test on that pointer plus a tail transfer, so the 'empty layout' case costs four instructions and never enters the scan.
The constant 0xeeee8218 is UTFWin::IWindow::TYPE, which pins the search's element filter to IWindow without any RTTI.
0x008105b0 ends in JMP, not CALL: it is a tail transfer, so a null-gate miss and a real scan share one stack frame and the arguments are forwarded in place.
The always-1 flag means the recursive variant is requested on both candidates; the SDK's default for that parameter is also true, so this is the common case rather than a special one.

Callers uniformly treat a non-null answer as a vtable-bearing UI object and dispatch slot +0x7c with (1, 1); eleven sibling callsites in FUN_005dda30 do this with four different control ids, which is what a control-id lookup table looks like.
The id argument is passed through a register (EDI) to both callsites, so the two searches always use the same id; there is no path where the fallback searches for something else.
unresolved_questions: The element array scanned by 0x00810200 lives at +0x64..+0x68 of the layout-objects target, but the SDK declares UILayoutObjects::mRootComponents at +0x5c. Either the SDK offsets for that class are wrong, or the scanned array is a different member. Not reconciled.

What do vtable slots +0x0c, +0x1c and +0xf0 do on a UTFWin element? The 0xEEEE8218 argument makes +0x0c a cast/filter, but neither the other two is named. The id compared at +0x1c is probably a control id, but that is an inference from the argument the callers pass.
Is slot +0xf0 a recursive descent into children, or a lookup in a sibling container? Its (id, 1) shape is consistent with both.

Is the flag argument ever 0 for this function? Both call sites here hard-code 1, and all 25 recorded callers route through those two sites, so the non-recursive path may be dead in this build. Not proven, because 0x008105b0 has other callers that were not enumerated.

What are the control ids 0x630c829, 0x578ec50, 0xf006efa5, 0xb006ef6e and 0x1140129d? None is named in the SDK. 0x578EC50 appears as a comment on an unrelated EditorUI field, which is suggestive and unproven.
The other 14 of the 25 callers were not inspected, so the argument distribution across the fan-in is not established.
Is 0x005dc310 itself an interface method or a vtable entry? No vtable was located for the EditorUI aggregate and no pointer scan for this address was performed.
confidence_note: confidence in the per-aspect claim, not a probability of behavioural equivalence with any shipped source

sdk_correspondence.observation: Spore/UTFWin/UILayout.h declares 'IWindow* FindWindowByID(uint32_t controlID, bool bRecursive = true);' with the documentation 'Returns the first child window that has the given controlID. By default, this also checks on the children's children.' The observed body matches that shape exactly: a 32-bit id, a bool that is always 1, a class filter on UTFWin::IWindow::TYPE = 0xEEEE8218, an equality test on an id returned through a virtual, and a second attempt through a virtual taking (id, 1) when the first fails. Spore/Editors/EditorUI.h declares mMainUI at +0x14 and mSharedUI at +0x2c and Spore/UTFWin/UILayout.h gives ASSERT_SIZE(UILayout, 0x18), which is the observed spacing.
sdk_correspondence.not_asserted: The name FindWindowByID is NOT claimed as this function's identity. The receiver here is the EditorUI aggregate that owns two layouts, and no SDK class declares a method that spans two of them; 0x005dc310 is at 0x005dc310, far from the UILayout code region. The SDK correspondence is recorded for the operation the two 0x008105b0 calls perform, not for this wrapper.
